title: Syntax and Meaning in NLP
description: Explore tagging, parsing, semantics, and information extraction.

questions.prompt: What does part-of-speech tagging assign to tokens?
options: Grammatical categories such as noun or verb
A sentiment score for the document
questions.explanation: POS tagging labels tokens with grammatical categories based on form and context.

questions.prompt: Which is a named-entity recognition task?
options: Identify a person, organization, or location mention
questions.explanation: NER locates and classifies spans such as people, organizations, and places.

questions.prompt: Named-entity recognition includes identifying entity boundaries as well as entity types.
questions.explanation: A system must determine which tokens form each mention and assign an appropriate label.

questions.prompt: What does a dependency parse represent?
options: Directed arcs linking dependents to heads
questions.explanation: Dependency structure links words through directed syntactic relations, commonly organizing dependents under heads in a tree.

questions.prompt: What does a constituency parse organize?
questions.explanation: Constituency parsing builds a hierarchical phrase structure such as noun and verb phrases.

questions.prompt: What is word-sense disambiguation?
options: Choosing the intended meaning of an ambiguous word in context
questions.explanation: Context helps distinguish senses of a form such as “bank” in financial and river contexts.

questions.prompt: A word can have multiple related senses depending on context.
questions.explanation: Polysemous words share related meanings, and context helps determine which sense is used.

questions.prompt: What is coreference resolution?
options: Determine which mentions refer to the same entity
Assign a language code to a document
questions.explanation: Coreference links mentions such as a name and a later pronoun that refer to the same entity.

questions.prompt: What does semantic role labeling identify?
options: Who did what to whom, when, or where in a predicate frame
questions.explanation: Semantic roles label participants and circumstances associated with a predicate or event.

questions.prompt: Which outputs may a relation-extraction system produce?
options: A guarantee that the relation is causally true
questions.explanation: Systems can extract relation labels and evidence, but text extraction alone does not establish causal truth.

questions.prompt: What is document-level sentiment classification intended to predict?
options: An overall polarity or opinion category
questions.explanation: Sentiment classification estimates opinion polarity, often positive, negative, or neutral.

questions.prompt: A sentiment classifier can always infer sarcasm accurately from polarity words alone.
questions.explanation: Sarcasm depends on context and pragmatic cues that a simple word-polarity method may miss.

questions.prompt: What is a topic model commonly used to infer?
options: Latent themes reflected by word co-occurrence
The exact author of every document
The next byte in a file
questions.explanation: Topic models represent documents as mixtures of latent themes under assumptions about word distributions.

questions.prompt: What does a distributional word embedding encode?
options: A dense vector learned from patterns of word context
A full dictionary definition by guarantee
A unique vector independent of training
The word’s grammatical role in every sentence
questions.explanation: Embeddings capture statistical patterns from contexts and may encode semantic or syntactic similarities.

questions.prompt: Which cautions apply to word embeddings?
options: They can reflect societal biases in data
A single static vector may miss context-dependent meaning
questions.explanation: Embeddings inherit data patterns; vector similarity is not a complete semantic or causal explanation.

questions.prompt: What does a sentence-embedding cosine similarity score usually indicate?
options: Angular similarity between two vector representations
The probability the sentences are both true
The count of shared words only
questions.explanation: Cosine similarity compares vector directions; its semantic usefulness depends on the embedding model and task.

questions.prompt: In natural-language inference, what does entailment mean?
options: The hypothesis follows from the premise under the task interpretation
The premise and hypothesis share a word
questions.explanation: Entailment means the premise supports the hypothesis as true within the annotation framework.

questions.prompt: Negation scope can change the interpretation of a sentence.
questions.explanation: Which words fall under negation can determine whether a claim is asserted or denied.

questions.prompt: What does a semantic frame describe?
options: A situation type and its associated participant roles
questions.explanation: Frames capture structured situations and roles, such as a buyer, seller, goods, and money in a transaction.

questions.prompt: Why use annotation guidelines in a language dataset?
options: Specify how ambiguous cases are handled
questions.explanation: Guidelines improve consistency and make disagreements measurable, though annotation still involves judgment.
